title: Model catalog: runtime compatibility delta spec and deprecation escape hatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Clarify the minimum compatibility metadata and the scoped deprecation path for new community/open model weights entering the Redwood model catalog. This ticket defines a concise, machine-parseable compatibility delta spec and the operational "escape hatch" for unpinned variants that fail runtime or quality checks. Goal is to reduce onboarding ambiguity for PM/Eng/RE and enable automated routing/rollbacks in the serving runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Define a compatibility delta schema (CSV and JSON) that includes: model_architecture, tokenizer_id, expected_kv_cache_semantics, max_sequence_length, supported_quantizations, recommended_batching_profile, and minimal_inference_profile (latency P50/P95 on reference hardware)
Publish a human-readable onboarding checklist derived from the schema with 6 mandatory items and 3 optional helpers for experimental variants

Runtime must be able to make an automated decision using these metadata fields to: (a) route to fallback variant when core mismatch is detected, (b) refuse pinless deployment if critical fields missing

Acceptance tests: new open-model entry passes an eval battery (safety smoke tests + 3 user prompt families), latency regression < 10% vs catalog baseline for comparable size, and cost-per-token increase < 15%
Deprecation escape hatch implemented: soft-flag, 30 day notification, automatic traffic re-route to pinned sibling after 7 day auto-escalation if no remediation
Docs and runtime mapping changes merged (Confluence + runtime PR) and internal release note created
decisions: Use a small, fixed compatibility field set rather than an open-ended schema to minimize upstream burden; additional fields can be added as opt-ins
Treat tokenizer mismatch as a blocking incompatibility (requires explicit tokenization shim or pinned variant)
Quantization support will be annotated as boolean flags per quant format (int8, int4) with recommended fallback variants listed
tradeoffs: Minimal schema reduces onboarding friction but may not capture edge-case behaviors (e.g., custom KV cache semantics). We accept this and route such cases to a manual intake flow.
Automated deprecation/escape hatch reduces operational toil but risks false-positive deprecations for low-traffic models; mitigation: human-in-loop review for first 2 instances per quarter
Stricter acceptance thresholds prolong onboarding time but reduce production incidents - we prioritize catalog stability for public variants
